entities.summary:
Raynerius of Split was an Italian Camaldolese monk who became a pivotal figure in the religious and political landscape of the Mediterranean during the 12th century. Born in the 11th century and died on August 4, 1180, Raynerius rose through the ranks of the Church, becoming bishop of Cagli from 1156 to 1175 and then archbishop of Split, a position he held until his death. Raynerius' leadership played a significant role in shaping the religious and political climate of the region, particularly during the tumultuous years of the Fourth Crusade.

Raynerius' legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he was instrumental in the establishment of the Catholic Church's presence in the Balkans and the Mediterranean. His contributions to the Church's structure and governance also had a lasting impact on the development of ecclesiastical institutions in the region.

One of the most notable aspects of Raynerius' life was his role in the Fourth Crusade, which saw the sacking of Constantinople in 1204. Despite the controversy surrounding this event, Raynerius was a key figure in the Crusade's leadership, using his position to influence the actions of the Crusader army and shape the course of the conflict.

The legacy of Raynerius of Split continues to be felt today, with his contributions to the Church's history and governance remaining an important part of the region's cultural heritage.
